messages:
ben-cs: Hey team — customer hitting intermittent 500s on checkout. They gave request id `req_3f9b2a`. Can someone paste a minimal set of repro capture steps (HAR + console + curl) I can send them? Need instructions they can follow in Chrome.

alex-support: Yep. Short checklist below (minimal, low-friction):
1) Open Chrome Incognito (or regular) and go to the checkout flow.
2) Open DevTools (F12) -> Settings: enable 'Preserve log' in Network and Console. Also disable cache while DevTools is open.
3) Reproduce the error. When the 500 happens, right-click inside Network -> Save all as HAR with content.
4) In Console tab: right-click -> Save as... (save console logs). Attach both.
5) Find the failing request in Network, click it -> Headers. Copy request headers and response headers. Look for any `x-request-id` or `x-rw-reqid` we can correlate.

alex-support: Minimal curl template to reproduce (replace with actual method/path/body/headers):
```
curl 'https://api.redwood.example/checkout' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <their-api-key-if-applicable>' \
  -H 'x-request-id: req_3f9b2a' \
  --data-raw '{"cart_id":"...","payment_method":"..."}' \
  -v
```
Replace --data-raw with the payload from the Network request -> Payload tab. If it's a GET, omit the data.

alex-support: If the response is chunked or streaming, add `--no-buffer` and `-N` flags. For TLS troubleshooting add `-k` only if asked (insecure).

ben-cs: Nice — can you add how to grab the specific request headers for us to grep in logs?

mike-sre: Quick add: copy these three things from the failing request: `request url`, `status code`, and the full request/response headers. If you paste the request URL to us we can grep across our logs by the `x-request-id` or the URL path + timestamp. Also include the HAR filename and the approximate timestamp of the failure.

sophie-eng: One more tip for customers on slow/async errors: record a short video (phone is fine) showing the steps + the DevTools sidebar so we can see timing. It helps match client-side vs server-side.

alex-support: Upload instructions: drop the HAR + console logs + curl snippet into the support ticket (or our secure upload link: https://files.redwood.example/upload - paste the upload link in the ticket). Before upload, blacklist or remove any sensitive tokens/PII (API keys, full card numbers). If they can't remove tokens, ask them to redact and tell us exact header names so we can request redacted copies.

deploy-bot: Incident note: please include UTC timestamp of failure and region (if known).

ben-cs: Great, I'll send this to the customer. One last thing — if the customer can't produce a HAR (old Safari), what is the fallback?

alex-support: Fallbacks: 1) curl reproduction using the captured headers/body (works 9/10). 2) Browser network export (Chrome recommended). 3) If they only have screenshots, ask for the `request id` and timestamp so SRE can search server logs.

mike-sre: If you get the HAR, run `haralyzer` locally or we can ingest it. If the HAR isn't available, request the exact `x-request-id` and a timeframe +/- 2 minutes. We'll check backend traces.

ben-cs: Perfect, thanks all :thumbsup:

alex-support: Copy/paste friendly version I just sent to the ticket: "Steps to capture a minimal DevTools snapshot (Chrome): Incognito -> F12 -> Network & Console: check Preserve log -> Disable cache -> Reproduce -> Save network -> Save console -> Export failing request headers & payload -> Run the provided curl template -> Upload HAR+console+curl to ticket. Include request id and UTC timestamp."

sophie-eng: I'll stand by for the HAR if you want me to triage after upload.

ben-cs: Upload link and note added. Closing this thread for now — will reopen if we need more.
